events.description: A sudden bright flash at f4 (4.0 s) rapidly expands into a fireball with outward-propagating sparks and debris through f10 (7.0 s), peaking around f8–f9 (6.0–6.5 s), then begins to decay by f11 (7.5 s); the rapid onset, symmetric expansion, and ejection of incandescent fragments are consistent with a single explosive blast.

verification.reason: Frames f4–f10 show the classic progression of an explosion: instantaneous ignition (f4), fireball growth (f5–f7), peak with radial spark ejection (f8–f10). Candidate 0 (4.0–8.5) and candidate 1 (7.0–9.5) both overlap this core phase; however, f11 onward shows diminishing embers without new blast dynamics, so t_end is capped at 8.5 s (f13) to stay within clear explosive behavior—f13 (8.5 s) still shows active spark dispersion, while f14 (9.0 s) is already transitioning to residual plume. Candidates 2 and 3 extend beyond observable blast effects and are not supported as separate explosions.
